cf.title: Setting the number of digits after the decimal point with a psql's pset variable

input.subject: Setting the number of digits after the decimal point with a psql's pset variable

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support in the thread, and 645cb44c5 is cited as existing practice, so level 1b does not stop the proposal. The design is not settled. The commit message says "rounds" while the code truncates (standards-compat-1), no output format is excluded (standards-compat-2), and exponent notation, NaN and Infinity have no rule (maintenance-fit-2). The list needs to agree on these semantics before code review is useful.

brief.title: psql \pset n_decimals to limit digits after the decimal point
brief.problem: Ratios and percentages in psql output show more fractional digits than a reader needs. Wrapping each column in round() is slow and error prone in large queries. The author wants a quick display setting for interactive users, for example when reading metrics at a customer site or formatting tables for the mailing lists.
brief.proposed_design: psql gets a new \pset variable, n_decimals, that cuts float4, float8 and numeric columns to a fixed number of fractional digits at display time. The default "all" keeps current behaviour, and a negative value means "all". The change sits in the fe_utils print code, so it touches only client output, not query results.
user_visible_surface: New psql \pset option n_decimals, accepting "all" or an integer.
New status message: Number of decimals is "N".
Changed output of float4, float8 and numeric columns in psql when n_decimals is set.
New fields in fe_utils print options (src/include/fe_utils/print.h), visible to other frontend tools using that API.
author_claims: Commit message says values are rounded, but the author confirms in message #6 that the code truncates and he prefers it.
\pset is the right place for this kind of feature.
Nathan Bossart wants the same feature, and Bertrand Drouvot cites 645cb44c5 as a precedent.
brief.thread_state: Nathan Bossart supports the idea, and Bertrand Drouvot accepts it after citing a precedent, then reports a heap overflow, truncation, wrong output for 1e100, memory leaks and lax input parsing. The author fixed parsing, says he probably fixed the overflow, and promises a new patch; none is attached yet.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether output should truncate or round; commit message, docs and code disagree.
The proposal does not say how exponent notation, NaN and Infinity are shown.
The proposal does not say whether n_decimals applies to \copy, CSV, unaligned or other output formats, or to \gset values.
The proposal does not say how n_decimals interacts with numericlocale.
The proposal does not say whether it supports adding trailing zeros, e.g. 1 shown as 1.00.
The docs do not warn that displayed values differ from stored values.

prior_attempts.title: psql: Add \pset true/false
prior_attempts.quote: FWIW, I am -1 on the concept of enforcing output values for particular datatypes because that's not the job of psql, and it is easy to do that at query level (no comment about the existing \pset NULL stuff).
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers held that choosing display values for one data type is not a job for psql, because the user can already format values in the query. Robert Haas also did not want similar options added for other data types later. The final tally showed more -1 than +1 votes. Discussion of a more general output filter, either client-side or in the backend, reached no design, so Michael Paquier marked the patch rejected.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P5 set display strings for booleans; this proposal limits fractional digits of float4, float8 and numeric. Messages #2 and #5 cite 645cb44c5 as having since opened the door to per-type display options, and this proposal has a +1 in message #3.

objections.title: Truncation makes psql output disagree with round() and with stored values
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA sets n_decimals 2 and sees 9.99 for a value of 9.999. round(9.999, 2) in the same session returns 10.00, so the screen and the query disagree. A hit ratio of 99.996 shows as 99.99 and looks short of a 100% target that it nearly meets.
objections.argument: Message #6 confirms the code truncates and the author prefers that. The commit message says "rounds", and the docs say neither. A setting that changes how numbers are shown should match the rounding users already get from round() and from numeric-to-text casts, or say plainly that it does not. The docs hunk also has no warning that shown values differ from stored values.
objections.author_must_show: Will n_decimals round like round(), and if it truncates, how do the docs warn users that the shown value is not the stored value?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 confirms truncation, the commit message says "rounds", and the docs hunk says neither. Message #5 expected round() behaviour, so the disagreement is real, and a new patch version can settle it.

objections.title: Proposal does not say which output formats n_decimals affects
objections.failure_scenario: A user puts \pset n_decimals 2 in .psqlrc for interactive work. Later a cron job runs psql --csv or -A -t into a file that another tool loads. The exported numbers are cut to two digits with no error, and nobody sees it until reports disagree with the database.
objections.argument: The change sits in the shared print path used by aligned, unaligned, CSV, HTML and other formats, and by \o. The proposal does not say whether machine-readable formats are excluded, or how it treats \gset, \crosstabview and expanded mode. numericlocale has the same reach but only adds separators and drops no digits. A setting that loses data needs a clearer boundary than one that only changes layout.
objections.author_must_show: Does n_decimals apply to csv and unaligned output and to \gset, and if it does, how is a .psqlrc setting kept from changing scripted exports?

critic.reasoning: The proposal and the docs hunk name no output format, and the change sits in the shared fe_utils print code. \gset probably does not use that code, but the csv and unaligned case with a .psqlrc setting is a concrete failure.

objections.title: Client re-parses the server's text output for float and numeric
objections.failure_scenario: A user sets n_decimals 0 and runs a query that returns 1e100::float8, NaN, or Infinity. psql prints 1 for 1e100, as message #5 shows. Users of domains over numeric, or of extension numeric types, see no effect, because the code checks only three built-in OIDs.
objections.argument: The design edits strings in fe_utils by hand, based on assumptions about how the server writes float4, float8 and numeric: where the decimal point sits, exponent notation, special values, and how numericlocale changes the string. Any later change to those output functions, or to extra_float_digits behaviour, must also update print.c, and no test fails if that update is missed. The new fields in print.h become API that other frontend tools inherit.
objections.author_must_show: Which output forms of float4, float8 and numeric will the formatter handle, and what keeps it in step when server output functions change?

critic.reasoning: Message #5 shows 1e100 printed as 1, and the author agrees in message #6 that it needs work. The domain example is weak, because the server reports the base type OID for a domain column, but the string-editing concern stands.

objections.title: Per-type display option repeats the case rejected for \pset true/false
objections.failure_scenario: After n_decimals goes in, the next patches ask for date formats, interval styles, and boolean strings in \pset, each citing this one. Each adds a \pset option, a status message, tab completion, and print.h fields. Reviewers have no principle left for saying no.
objections.argument: [P5] was rejected because picking display values for one data type was held not to be psql's job when the query can do it, and because of worry about follow-on options for other types. Message #2 raised the same worry, then set it aside by citing 645cb44c5. That makes two precedents in favour, and the series gets easier to extend each time. A committer would likely ask for a general rule, or a general formatting hook, before adding another type-specific knob.
objections.author_must_show: What rule would decide which later per-type display options belong in \pset, and why does n_decimals fit it while \pset true/false did not?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 raised the follow-on worry and the thread answered it only by citing a commit, with no rule for later per-type options. [P5] must not be used as support, because psql has since accepted boolean display options.

objections.title: Demand rests on two users, and round() already covers the need
objections.failure_scenario: psql takes on a permanent \pset option, new fe_utils print fields, docs and tests for numeric display formatting. The only users shown are two developers who would otherwise add round() to their queries. Later requests for similar per-type display options cite this option as precedent.
objections.argument: The evidence of demand is the author's own consulting workflow (messages #1, #4) and one +1 from a developer who wanted it "a handful of times" (message #3). The thread cites no -general or -bugs reports and names no client tool that offers this. [P5] rejected per-type display values in psql because "it is easy to do that at query level", and round() is that query-level way here. Message #5 cites 645cb44c5 as precedent, but that shows only that the door is open, not that users want this.
objections.author_must_show: Which users beyond this thread ask for display-time decimal limits, and why does round() or a saved psql variable holding a query not serve them?

critic.reasoning: The thread shows two independent users, and round() can do the job, so the material does not show a common need. That is a "show demand" point, not a rejection, and [P5] must not be used as support.

refuted.title: Per-type display formatting in psql was rejected before for the same reason
refuted.failure_scenario: After n_decimals goes in, someone proposes display options for booleans, timestamps or intervals and cites n_decimals as the precedent. psql then has a growing set of per-type \pset knobs that format output on the client and duplicate what round() or to_char() already do in the query.
refuted.argument: [P5] proposed per-type display values in psql and was rejected because formatting one data type is "not the job of psql" and is easy at query level. Message #2 raises the same concern about other data types. Message #5 answers it only by pointing to 645cb44c5, and the thread does not say what that commit does or why it covers this case. The author's answer in message #1, that round() is error prone in large queries, is one side of the argument. It fits a per-type option for any type equally well.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is numeric precision different from the boolean display rejected earlier, and what keeps n_decimals from becoming the precedent for per-type options for every other type?

critic.reasoning: Messages #2 and #5 say 645cb44c5 already opened the door to per-type options, and psql now has \pset display_true and display_false. So the [P5] outcome no longer holds. The remaining follow-on worry is covered by maintenance-fit-1.

refuted.title: Display semantics split reviewers, as in the earlier JSON output attempt
refuted.failure_scenario: A user sets n_decimals 2 and reads 9.99 for a stored 9.999, while another user expects 10.00 as round() would give. Neither user can see from the output which rule applied, and changing the rule later changes every saved psqlrc's output.
refuted.argument: [P2] stalled because "different people want different corner-case behaviors" about numeric scale and float precision in psql output. The same split is already visible here. Message #5 expects rounding, message #6 chooses truncation, and the commit message says "rounds". Exponent notation, NaN, Infinity and trailing zeros have no stated rule yet.
refuted.author_must_show: Which rule, truncation or rounding, will n_decimals use for numeric, float4, float8, exponent notation and NaN, and why will users accept it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which states the truncation and rounding conflict more directly. [P2] concerned a JSON output format and round-trip safety, so it adds no support here.

refuted.title: Per-type display formatting was rejected before, and corner cases are not decided
refuted.failure_scenario: After this goes in, users ask for the same control over timestamps, intervals, money and booleans, and each one needs its own \pset. Users of n_decimals meanwhile disagree about exponent form, NaN, Infinity and trailing zeros, which the proposal leaves open.
refuted.argument: [P5] rejected \pset true/false because forcing display values for one data type was "not the job of psql" and is easy to do in the query. That reason applies here, since round() exists. Message #2 shows the same worry about more per-type options, settled only by a reference to 645cb44c5. [P2] stalled because people wanted different corner-case behavior, and message #5 shows 1e100 printed as 1, with no rule yet for exponent output.
refuted.author_must_show: How does this differ from the rejected \pset true/false, and what defined output will exponent notation, NaN, Infinity and integer-valued numerics get?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1 for the per-type part, and of standards-compat-1 and maintenance-fit-2 for the corner cases. It adds no new point.

refuted.title: Query-level round() or a numeric cast already gives this result
refuted.failure_scenario: psql gains a permanent \pset option that only saves typing round(x, 2) or x::numeric(10,2). Later proposals for date, boolean or interval display options can then point to n_decimals as precedent, and each one adds its own help text, tab completion and print.h fields. Reviewers meet that pressure with every such patch.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says round() does the job and is easy for simple queries, so the gap is convenience in large queries. Messages #2 and #5 show the same worry about other data types, settled by pointing to 645cb44c5. [P5] was rejected for this reason: per-type display values are easy at query level and are not psql's job. \pset numericlocale already formats numbers, which weakens this point, so a committer would likely weigh the demand.
refuted.author_must_show: Beyond typing round() per column, what does n_decimals give that a query cannot, and why would it not justify similar \pset options for other types?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1 for the round() argument and of maintenance-fit-1 for the follow-on options. Its [P5] support is outdated.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds fields to the print options in src/include/fe_utils/print.h, which other frontend tools use.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: Truncation makes psql output disagree with round() and with stored values

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: The patch adds \pset n_decimals, a status message, help text and tab completion, and changes how float4, float8 and numeric are shown.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: print.c edits the server's text output for float4, float8 and numeric, so it must follow any change to those output functions.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: Message #1 says round() in the query already gives the result; the option adds convenience for large queries.

questions: Will n_decimals round as round() does or truncate, and will the commit message, docs and code say the same thing?
Does n_decimals apply to csv, unaligned and \o output, and how is a .psqlrc setting kept from changing scripted exports?
What does n_decimals show for exponent notation such as 1e100, for NaN and for Infinity?
How does n_decimals interact with numericlocale, and does it add trailing zeros so that 1 shows as 1.00?
What rule decides which later per-type display options belong in \pset, so that n_decimals is not the argument for each one?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows psql and the fe_utils print code would have to own it. The visible thread shows support for the idea but nobody offering to commit it.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a permanent \pset option and for client code that edits the server's float and numeric text output. That code needs an update whenever those output functions change.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered the review, fixed input parsing and promised a new patch version; none is attached yet.

priority.reason: The patch is about 9 KiB and stays in psql and fe_utils, and the thread shows two interactive users who want it. Rounding, the output formats covered and the special values need a decision before another review round.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so this review cannot say which output formats the print.c change reaches or how it handles numericlocale. The heap overflow and memory leaks reported in the thread are implementation matters and were not judged.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql markdown output format
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add new psql output formats, mainly markdown and rst, selectable with \pset format, so query results can be pasted into wikis, Sphinx documents and GitHub issues. The patch reused the aligned format code and added markdown-specific width and formatting functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not post a new version after Fabien COELHO's May 2017 review, and the entry moved through two commitfests waiting on the author. That review found no defined markdown variant, incomplete escaping of markdown special characters, U+2502 characters leaking in from the unicode linestyle, and duplicated code paths. Michael Paquier returned it with feedback after no update for about six weeks, and the author confirmed he had no progress.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It's been 1 month and a half since this last status, and no updates have showed up.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql JSON output format
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a JSON output format to psql (\pset format json, psql --json/-J) that renders query results as an array of objects, with a compact layout in normal mode and a one-key-per-line layout in expanded mode. Later versions printed numeric and boolean values without quotes and json values as quoted strings, so that SQL NULL and JSON null could be told apart and the output would round-trip for a planned \gedit feature.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers disagreed on corner-case behavior and no agreement was reached. The open questions were how to tell SQL NULL apart from JSON null, whether json/jsonb values should be embedded as JSON or quoted as strings, and how much round-trip safety to require (numeric scale, float precision, array bounds). The last patch version from January 22 drew several replies but no newer version followed, and Robert Haas marked the entry Returned with Feedback. He suggested settling on one behavior everyone could accept or adding a short list of options.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMHO, the big problem here is that different people want different
corner-case behaviors and it's not clear what to do about that.

precedents_retrieved.title: csv output format for psql
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a CSV output format to psql (\pset format csv, plus a --csv command-line option) that applies CSV quoting rules to query and meta-command output, as an alternative to COPY/\copy for producing CSV. Later versions introduced a separate fieldsep_csv variable defaulting to a comma, with validation of allowed separator values.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because, after the last review in late August 2018, the patch was waiting for a response from the author and no new version was posted. Earlier disagreements over field-separator handling appear to have been settled by the fieldsep_csv design, which Pavel Stehule accepted; the last review asked for an added test for rejected fieldsep_csv values.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch has been waiting for input from the author since August, so I
am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: make psql backslash commands honor "\pset null"
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the special handling of NULL values in psql backslash commands, which set nullPrint = NULL in src/bin/psql/describe.c. Commands such as \dp would then honor "\pset null", so a NULL ACL (default privileges) can be told apart from an empty one.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch on the day he posted it, after he saw that a conflicting proposal existed and said he would reply on that thread. No one objected to the patch in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I just realize that there is a conflicting proposal.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: Add \pset true/false
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `\pset true` and `\pset false` to psql, so the user can choose the strings shown for boolean values in place of the default t/f. It works like the existing `\pset null` option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers held that choosing display values for one data type is not a job for psql, because the user can already format values in the query. Robert Haas also did not want similar options added for other data types later. The final tally showed more -1 than +1 votes. Discussion of a more general output filter, either client-side or in the backend, reached no design, so Michael Paquier marked the patch rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
FWIW, I am -1 on the concept of enforcing output values for particular
datatypes because that's not the job of psql, and it is easy to do
that at query level (no comment about the existing \pset NULL stuff).

precedents_retrieved.title: psql - possibility to specify where status row should be displayed
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new psql variable, STATUS_TARGET, would let the user send command status rows (such as "INSERT 0 1") to the terminal while \o redirects query results elsewhere. The motivating setup is psql in one terminal and a pager such as pspg reading results from a fifo in another.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Artur Zakirov suggested that the existing QUIET variable already hides status messages and covers more cases. Pavel Stehule replied that he wants to see the status row, but no one reviewed the patch for about eight months after that. David Steele then proposed closing it for lack of reviewer or committer interest, and the author agreed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's been quite a while since the patch has seen any review. It's not
clear that this is enough of an improvement over QUIET to be worthwhile.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql \graw execution and output format
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a psql command \graw (and \graw+) that runs the current query and prints the result in a new minimal raw output format, so it can be piped straight into tools such as gnuplot or R. The patch added a new print format and a flag to optionally include column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO's review found that the patch had no help entry, regression tests or documentation. He also questioned whether a new column_header flag and a separate print function were needed, rather than reusing tuples_only and the unaligned format. Pavel Stehule replied that the patch was a proof of concept for checking usability and design, and that he would wait for a later commitfest for more ideas, tests and feedback. The visible messages do not include a closing message stating the reason for the Returned with feedback outcome.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: yes - I wrote it like proof concept - be possible (for me, for others) to verify usability of this commands (and design).

precedents_retrieved.title: Precision loss casting float to numeric
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Robert Haas, Bear Giles
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make the float4 and float8 to numeric casts keep full binary precision, so that the cast and the round trip back to float no longer lose bits. The proof-of-concept patch printed values with FLT_DECIMAL_DIG and DBL_DECIMAL_DIG digits in place of FLT_DIG and DBL_DIG, and the author planned a frexp-based conversion.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and Robert Haas expected more complaints about results such as 1.1::float8 casting to an odd-looking numeric than benefit from exact values, and Bear Giles asked that existing results not change. Making the cast follow extra_float_digits would make it stable instead of immutable. Per-schema casts cannot work because casts have no names, which left a separate named function as the remaining option. The author marked the entry Returned with feedback, citing the backward-compatibility issues and lack of time in this CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think there's probably a bigger chance of complaints that "casting 1.1::float8 to numeric now produces some weird, incorrectly-rounded result" than that we make anyone happier.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert support for improved tracking of nested queries
Reverted commit(s): Track more precisely query locations for nested statements; Fix regression with location calculation of nested statements; pg_stat_statements: Add tests for nested queries with level tracking
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the two following commits:
- 499edb09741b, track more precisely query locations for nested
statements.
- 06450c7b8c70, a follow-up fix of 499edb09741b with query locations.
The test introduced in this commit is not reverted.  This is proving
useful to track a problem that only pgaudit was able to detect.

These prove to have issues with the tracking of SELECT statements, when
these use multiple parenthesis which is something supported by the
grammar.  Incorrect location and lengths are causing pg_stat_statements
to become confused, failing its job in query normalization with
potential out-of-bound writes because the location and the length may
not match with what can be handled.  A lot of the query patterns
discussed when this issue was reported have no test coverage in the main
regression test suite, or the recovery test 027_stream_regress.pl would
have caught the problems as pg_stat_statements is loaded by the node
running the regression tests.  A first step would be to improve the test
coverage to stress more the query normalization logic.

A different portion of this work was done in 45e0ba30fc40, with the
addition of tests for nested queries.  These can be left in the tree.
They are useful to track the way inner queries are currently tracked by
PGSS with non-top-level entries, and will be useful when reconsidering
in the future the work reverted here.

roaster_notes.note: Two objections are raised, both rooted in precedents whose reasons the thread has not yet answered.

The proposal changes only how psql displays float4, float8 and numeric values, so it creates no on-disk, WAL, catalog, replication or wire-protocol state. The new fields in fe_utils print.h are in a static frontend library, not a server ABI that extensions link against, so they need no backpatch or ABI care.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. n_decimals is a psql display setting that changes only how the client prints values it has already received.
